molecules.title: Molecules: Mena-LAM-s (lam5-v1)
molecules.body: Molecules run on Mena-LAM-s by default (35 MB, loads in about 60 ms). Besides energies and forces it predicts partial charges, the dipole and the polarizability, which give IR & Raman spectra, and includes D3(BJ) dispersion. Fused GPU kernels and a low-memory CPU mode run biomolecules of thousands of atoms on a laptop.

materials.badge: Default for crystals and surfaces · Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1)
materials.title: Periodic materials: Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1)
materials.body: Crystals and surfaces run on Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1, 34 MB, strict IEEE FP32) by default: Matbench Discovery CPS 0.874, F1 0.904, κ_SRME 0.182 (0/103 imaginary modes), WBM-257k in 4m 38s, DynaMat MD in 43.6 min (0.46 GB VRAM, #1 active speed), 555.3k atoms/s on RTX PRO 6000 (Si 32k) and 98.6k atoms/s on Apple M3 Max (Si 8k), plus OC20/OC25/MAD-1.6 catalysis support and physics interpretation heads. Earlier Mena-LAM-preview (lam-400k: F1 0.905, CPS 0.849, DynaMat MD CMDS 0.787) and Mena-LAM-s (lam5-v1: 65,895–130,348 atoms/s at 8,000 silicon atoms and 64,000 atoms in 3.7 GB on Apple M3 Max) can also be chosen in Settings.

tier2_scaling.title: Molecular scaling on an Apple M3 Max (36 GB): fused GPU kernels vs. plain PyTorch
tier2_scaling.badge: Up to 12.5× faster · 9.9× lower GPU memory
tier2_scaling.note: The fused path runs message passing, exact Coulomb and D3 dispersion as Metal GPU kernels with constant extra memory. At 8,192 atoms it runs 29,808 atoms/s in 2.69 GB of GPU memory (1.28 GB in low-memory mode); plain PyTorch needs 13.9 GB at 4,096 atoms and runs out of memory at 8,192.
tier2_scaling.source: Measured on an Apple M3 Max (36 GB) on 2026-11-12, one process per size: energy and forces with a 0.6 Å neighbour skin and MD-like moves. Memory is what each run needs: the least Metal GPU memory it reached with the allocator limited (with memory free, PyTorch's allocator keeps freed blocks and the peak is higher). Speeds are with memory free.

cpu_and_workflows.title: CPU low-memory mode (0.17 MB/atom) and batched GPU workflows

facts.CPU drug single-point: 17.1–39.2 ms (~15–45 ms: H₂O 17.1 ms, caffeine 29.4 ms, ibuprofen 39.2 ms)
facts.CPU low-memory mode (3,000 atoms): +0.50 GB net / 0.89 GB total (0.17 MB/atom, measured 2026-11-12)
facts.GPU eval_batch (64× drugs, N=18–92): 329.4 structs/s on M3 Max GPU (4.44× faster than plain PyTorch, 74.3)
facts.GPU eval_batch (32× pockets, N=200–310): 64.3 structs/s in 0.74 GB (6.77× faster, 4.9× lower RAM)
facts.GPU relax_batch (24× L-BFGS, 35 steps): 2.45 s = 9.80 relax/s (30.05× faster than 73.60 s serial ASE)
facts.Caffeine Hessian + IR + Raman: 0.508 s for 144 displacements (3.53 ms/disp, 10.86× faster than 5.52 s CPU serial)
facts.FAIRChem OMol25 full runs on M3 Max: GEOM Conformers (8,245 relax) in 29.3 min (beats Cloud A100 31.2 min); Ligand Strain in 38.1 min (vs. 49.0 min A100)

cpu_and_workflows.source: Measured on an Apple M3 Max (36 GB).

accuracy_and_spectroscopy.title: Molecular accuracy, electrostatics & spectroscopy highlights (Mena-LAM-s)

facts.TorsionNet500 (DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS): 0.205 kcal/mol barrier MAE (R² = 0.9802; 12,000 pts in 10.8 s = 1,111 structs/s)
facts.Wiggle150 strained conformers: 1.066 kcal/mol MAE (R² = 0.9971; ahead of ωB97M-D3BJ/QZVP 1.18 & AIMNet2 2.35)
facts.OMol25 S2EF val_sub5k & Biomolecules: 1.640 kcal/mol E / 0.340 kcal/mol/Å F; Val-Comp Biomolecules 53.87 meV (UMA-M-1.1: 58.65)
facts.Dipole & polarizability (def2-TZVPD): Neutral dipole r = 0.9997 (MAE 0.009 e·Å); α_iso scaling r = 0.9955; Raman anisotropy γ r = 0.967
facts.QVib 1,366 conformers & IR spectra: Freq MAE 5.58 cm⁻¹ vs. PBE0+MBD (4.43 vs. ωB97M-V); IR cosine 0.8761 (matches MACE-POLAR-1 0.8765); Born charges r = 0.9993

accuracy_and_spectroscopy.source: PLF547, TorsionNet500, Folmsbee, Wiggle150, GMTKN55, OMol25 validation and QVib benchmarks.

hardware_banner.title: Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1) strict IEEE FP32 on RTX PRO 6000 & Apple M3 Max laptop vs. H100 / H200 / Blackwell / H20
hardware_banner.mena_tag: Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1): 1× RTX PRO 6000 / Apple M3 Max laptop (strict FP32)
hardware_banner.other_tag: Competitors: NVIDIA H100 / H200 / RTX PRO 6000 / H20 96 GB
hardware_banner.dynamat: On the official Matbench Discovery DynaMat v1.0 MD benchmark (17 crystals × 80,000 NVT steps = 210M atom-steps), Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1) ran in strict IEEE FP32 on 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell in 0.726 h (43.6 min, 2,614 s) with 0.46 GB peak VRAM and CMDS 0.777 (CPS 0.874) — #1 fastest active model on the leaderboard (4.8× faster than DPA-4.1-Air-OAM at 3.52 h / 1.33 GB on the same RTX PRO 6000, and 3.6× faster than ORB v2 MPA at 2.61 h on H200). Earlier Mena-LAM-preview (lam-400k, A100: 2.37 h, 0.72 GB, CMDS 0.787) is retained in the charts for comparison.
hardware_banner.diamond: DPA4 dense-diamond test (158 neighbours per atom at 6 Å; energy, forces and stress), measured on an Apple M3 Max laptop (36 GB, 300 GB/s): Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1) runs 37,735 atoms/s (37.7 atoms/ms) at 32,768 atoms with 0.049 MB/atom live GPU memory (0.038 MB/atom low-memory; 37,244 atoms/s and 0.054 MB/atom at 13,824 atoms), while Mena-LAM-s (lam5-v1) runs 46,188 atoms/s at 32,768 atoms (0.052 MB/atom live). All competing models were reported on an NVIDIA H20 96 GB server GPU (4,000 GB/s) in the DPA4 paper.

lam6_materials_benchmarks.title: Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1): 5-Pillar Matbench Discovery & Solid-State Benchmarks

facts.Combined Performance (CPS): 0.8739 (48.5 GPU-h on 1× RTX PRO 6000; #16 overall, matches SevenNet-Omni & MACE-SOYO-OAM, beats NequIP-OAM-L 0.870 & ORB v3 0.861)
facts.Discovery (WBM-257k, uniq.): F1 = 0.9037, MAE = 20.56 meV/atom, DAF = 5.937, 0/256,963 fails (all 256,963 relaxed in 278.2 s = 923.6 cryst/s, 2.26 GB VRAM)
facts.Phonons (PhononDB-103): κ_SRME = 0.1824 (−40.5% vs. lam-400k), 0/103 imaginary modes, spectrum w1 = 0.1153 THz
facts.Geometry Optimization: RMSD = 0.0623 Å, 81.89% symmetry match (moyopy symprec=1e-2; 69.17% at 1e-5)
facts.DynaMat MD (CMDS, 17×80k): CMDS = 0.7770 (#2 active) in 2,613.9 s (43.6 min, #1 active speed), 0.456 GB peak VRAM
facts.Diatomics (CDS, 92×119): CDS = 0.7606 (+0.244 vs. lam-400k) in 21.1 s (518.6 calls/s, 0.199 GB VRAM), 80/81 vib freq
facts.MDR-442 & X23 crystals: MDR-442 Hessian col.rel = 0.044 (−58% vs. lam-400k); X23 = 7.69 kJ/mol (ML-PEG 0.9231)

lam6_materials_benchmarks.note: Single 7.98M-param checkpoint evaluated in strict IEEE FP32 (allow_tf32=False, zero BF16/FP16) with lot='mp' + MP2020 +U, validated in upstream matbench-discovery.
lam6_materials_benchmarks.source: Matbench Discovery 5-task evaluation (2026-11-20 & 2026-11-22 RTX PRO 6000), MDR-442, X23, and STFC ML-PEG.

lam6_speed_scaling.title: Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1) crystal speed & memory scaling (strict IEEE FP32 & CPU FP64)
lam6_speed_scaling.badge: 555.3k at/s RTX PRO 6000 · 98.6k at/s M3 Max
lam6_speed_scaling.note: Dual-CSR register-streaming kernels (CUDA C++, Apple Metal, OpenMP C++) eliminate [E, C] edge buffers (O(N) live memory). On RTX PRO 6000, lam6-v1 beats FACTO-OAM-S (429.5k at/s in BF16×3) by 1.29× in strict IEEE FP32.
lam6_speed_scaling.source: Measured 2026-11-22 on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB, CUDA 13.0) and Apple M3 Max (36 GB, 40-core GPU / 10 P-cores).

Automatic uses Mena-LAM-6 (lam6-v1) for crystals; pick Mena-LAM-s (or Mena-LAM-preview) in Settings for these speeds.
